Container.Name: keystone
Container.Overview: Keystone — self-hosted multi-tenant personal financial platform (FastAPI + PostgreSQL 16 + Next.js). Consumes market/account data from Tape via its API (Keystone does not talk to Schwab directly). ONE neutral template for dev and prod: at creation set Name (keystone / keystone-dev), image tag (:stable / :dev), network mode / static IP, DB host + the TWO DB logins (owner DB_* + non-owner APP_DB_*), the Tape base URL, and secrets. TWO DB logins are required (keystone#14): migrations run as the owner (DB_*), the app runs as a non-owner app_role member (APP_DB_*) so row-level security is enforced — the container fails closed if the app login is missing. The DB connection is assembled internally from the discrete variables (no baked DATABASE_URL). Start the keystone-db container FIRST; the entrypoint runs migrations, then serves. Deploy check: GET /v1/health reports release/sha plus db and tape reachability.
Container.Description: Keystone — multi-tenant personal financial platform. Neutral template; set Name (keystone / keystone-dev), IP, image tag, DB host/password, Tape URL, and secrets at creation.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: App HTTP port (FastAPI/gunicorn)

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: App data (encrypted file vault). REQUIRED - an absolute path on a POOL, NOT the user-share FUSE overlay.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the nightly pg_dump lands (KW-SELF-BACKUP-1). REQUIRED for a real backup: WITHOUT this mount the dump is written INSIDE the container and destroyed by the next update — the job still reports success, which is exactly the failure mode tape hit for months before its own Backups mount existed. Set an absolute path on a POOL DIFFERENT from the one holding the DB container's data (e.g. /mnt/<other-pool>/appdata/keystone/backups), so one pool failure cannot take both the database and its only backup. The app WARNS in the container log at boot and at every dump if this path is not a persistent mount. ⚠️ THIS MOUNT IS THE BACKUP DESTINATION — there is deliberately no separate Variable for it, because the two must never disagree: a Variable pointing anywhere other than this mount point would send dumps into the container filesystem, which is the exact silent failure above.

Config.Name: DB_HOST
Config.Description: PostgreSQL host — the keystone-db container's IP (set at creation). Shared by the owner and app logins.

Config.Name: DB_PORT
Config.Description: PostgreSQL port

Config.Name: DB_USER
Config.Description: OWNER DB login — owns the tables and runs migrations (alembic). Should be a NON-superuser so FORCE row-level security binds it too.

Config.Name: DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Password for the OWNER login DB_USER (matches the role you created on keystone-db).

Config.Name: DB_NAME
Config.Description: PostgreSQL database name

Config.Name: APP_DB_USER
Config.Description: APPLICATION (runtime) DB login — the NON-owner identity gunicorn connects as (keystone#14). Must be a member of app_role with NO BYPASSRLS and must NOT own tables, or RLS is bypassed. Create on keystone-db: CREATE ROLE keystone_app LOGIN PASSWORD '...' NOSUPERUSER INHERIT; GRANT app_role TO keystone_app;

Config.Name: APP_DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Password for the APP login APP_DB_USER (the non-owner app_role member). Required whenever DB_HOST is set — the container fails closed without it rather than running as the owner.

Config.Name: BACKUP_DB_USER
Config.Description: BACKUP DB login — the identity the nightly pg_dump connects as. Must have its own BYPASSRLS attribute (a migration cannot set this; it is not inheritable) AND be a member of backup_role for schema-wide SELECT. Create on keystone-db: CREATE ROLE keystone_backup LOGIN PASSWORD '...' NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS; GRANT backup_role TO keystone_backup;

Config.Name: BACKUP_DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Password for the BACKUP login BACKUP_DB_USER. Left blank, the nightly backup job still starts and every dump fails to log in (logged as a failed nightly dump). Blanking BACKUP_DB_USER does not stop it: Unraid passes that Variable's Default, keystone_backup, when it is blank. The app still serves normally.

Config.Name: TRUSTED_PROXIES
Config.Description: Comma-separated IPs/CIDRs of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For header may be trusted (e.g. the proxy container's address or its subnet). SET THIS if Keystone is reached through a reverse proxy, or per-IP rate limiting collapses into a single shared bucket for every visitor and auth audit rows record the proxy instead of the client. Leave blank when the container is reached directly.

Config.Name: TAPE_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Base URL of the Tape deployment THIS instance consumes — e.g. http://<tape-host>:8000 or https://tape-dev.your-domain.example. NOTE: Tape validates the Host header (its TRUSTED_HOSTS variable) — the host/IP in this URL must be on THAT allowlist or Tape answers 400.

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_ID
Config.Description: Per-service client id registered on the Tape side (the keystone-backend entry; scopes market,account). Keystone authenticates to Tape with this pair (app/tape_client.py) — a blank pair fails at the first Tape call rather than at boot.

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET
Config.Description: Secret paired with TAPE_CLIENT_ID (minted on the Tape side).

Config.Name: TAPE_API_KEY
Config.Description: LEGACY shared key honored by pre-enforcement Tape deployments only; sent as X-API-Key alongside the client-id pair (app/tape_client.py) — leave blank once Tape enforces its client registry.

Config.Name: JWT_SECRET_KEY
Config.Description: Signing secret for JWT access + MFA step tokens — ONE key (refresh 'rotation' issues a new token, not a second signing key). MINIMUM 32 characters, ENFORCED: shorter (or blank) and every auth endpoint answers 503 fail-closed. Generate: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"

Config.Name: FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
Config.Description: AES-256 (base64 Fernet) key for the file vault (personal documents at rest) — also the local KMS service key wrapping stored secrets (TOTP MFA seeds). Blank = MFA enrollment answers 503. Generate: python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"

Config.Name: ADMIN_MFA_RESET
Config.Description: BREAK-GLASS, LAST RESORT — leave BLANK in normal operation. Any non-empty, non-"0" value ARMS a ONE-SHOT reset, on the NEXT container start, of the single account named by ADMIN_RECOVERY_EMAIL: its MFA is cleared to 'pending', the authenticator secret is WIPED, its recovery codes are dropped, its live sessions are revoked, and a RANDOM temporary password is written to the CONTAINER LOG (never stored here, so it cannot be read back off the container config) with a forced change on first login. The value itself is just a marker — use anything, e.g. a date — and the reset fires ONCE PER DISTINCT VALUE, so a restart while it is still set will NOT reset the account a second time; set a NEW value to re-arm. While this is non-blank the container logs a WARNING on EVERY start, because a standing break-glass Var is a standing operator backdoor. CLEAR IT TO 0 (or blank) once you are back in.

Config.Name: ADMIN_RECOVERY_EMAIL
Config.Description: BREAK-GLASS, LAST RESORT — leave BLANK in normal operation. The email address of the ONE admin/owner account ADMIN_MFA_RESET is allowed to reset; no other account can be touched by it, and a blank value makes the reset a no-op even when ADMIN_MFA_RESET is set. Example: owner@example.com

Config.Name: ALLOW_UNSAFE_DB_POSTURE
Config.Description: Leave BLANK (safe). At start the app reads its OWN database identity and REFUSES TO BOOT if that login is a superuser, has BYPASSRLS, or is not a member of app_role — all three bypass row-level security, so tenant isolation would be silently OFF while /v1/health still reported ok. Set to 1 ONLY to deliberately run on a single-role database, or to unblock a false-positive detection: the refusal becomes a loud WARNING and the container boots with tenant isolation UNENFORCED. The correct fix is almost always APP_DB_USER — point it at the non-owner app_role login, not the owner or the bootstrap superuser.

Config.Name: LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: App log level (debug/info/warning/error)

Config.Name: WEB_CONCURRENCY
Config.Description: Gunicorn worker count (Keystone scales with workers; no shared-upstream pin like Tape)
